name: NUMAlloc
baseline: mimalloc, glibc malloc, TcMalloc, Intel TBB
workload: Application benchmark suite on NUMA machines (ISMM 2023 paper).
claimed_speedup: 15.7% faster than the second-best allocator (mimalloc) and 20.9% faster than the default Linux allocator (a patent summary snippet gives 15.2% and 17.1%).
tradeoffs: NUMA-aware; reasonable memory overhead per paper; README lists planned work such as removing callsite info collection.
caveats: Peer-reviewed ISMM 2023 paper, ACM page blocked so numbers are from search snippets and differ between sources; license not confirmed on repo page I read.
found_via: WebSearch: NUMAlloc github utsasrg paper ISMM 2023 faster than mimalloc tcmalloc

name: fmtlog
claimed_speedup: Named among the fastest libraries in both scenarios (with Nanolog, quill, haclog) versus spdlog, glog, loguru, easyloggingpp and reckless; results shown only as charts, no table of numbers on the page.
tradeoffs: Fastest mode drops logs when the buffer is full; blocking mode loses speed.
caveats: Independent single-machine laptop run; numbers are in SVG charts and report text files, not quoted here; flags not stated; not all scenarios covered for fmtlog, quill and reckless per the author.

name: Quill

tradeoffs: Bounded queue mode used for the test; bounded blocking mode got stuck in scenario 1 and was skipped.

name: runtime-benchmarks (tzcnt)
baseline: oneTBB, Taskflow (OpenMP and Rayon not included)
workload: Cross-runtime fork-join suite: skynet, nqueens, fib(39), matmul(2048) on 64 cores, ten C++ runtimes.
claimed_speedup: libfork skynet 36,519 us, nqueens 69,010 us, fib(39) 62,367 us, matmul(2048) 44,140 us; oneTBB and Taskflow showed mean ratios of 3.25x and 3.34x versus the best performer.
tradeoffs: Benchmark suite only; winners are libfork and TooManyCooks (both already catalogued), citor is listed too.
caveats: Evidence for known projects (libfork, TooManyCooks) and for citor. Page says a LICENSE file exists but SPDX not read; last commit date not shown. Maintained by the TooManyCooks author, so not fully independent.
found_via: GitHub: WebSearch 'work-stealing scheduler C++ library benchmark vs OpenMP TBB fork-join fibonacci github'
